title: Speed Humps
summary: Standard details for Type I (12 ft long) and Type II (22 ft long) asphalt speed humps, their chevron markings, and the advance warning sign and HUMPS pavement legend. Humps are installed only when authorized by LADOT. Finished height is 2 5/8 inches with a +1/4 inch tolerance, and humps stay 5 ft or more from driveways and catch basins. Sheet 1 shows sign and hump placement on two-lane streets and streets with a striped median.

sheets.notes:
Layout on Two-Lane Street (Type I marking shown, see Sheet 4 for Type II)
Signs W17-1 and W13-1(15) at each approach, see Note 5. Spacing between humps 100' to 250' (and 250' to 600' as shown). Hump length 12' or 22'.

Layout on Street with Striped Median (Type I marking shown, see Sheet 4 for Type II)
Signs W17-1 and W13-1(15) at each approach, see Note 5. Hump length 12' or 22'. Type I or Type II asphalt hump.

Section A-A
Curb face width varies. A.C. standard 3/8 aggregate mix. If there is no actual gutter, use 2' from flow line.

Advance Warning Sign
30" x 30" W17-1 modified, with Type II-A retro-reflective sheeting.
24" x 24" W13-1(15), with Type II-A retro-reflective sheeting.
Sign post 12" min. from curb face. Mounting height 7' min.

Advance Pavement Marking (see S-509.0)
HUMPS legend placed in the lane between the geometric or striped centerline (or solid yellow line of a striped median) and the curb face or flow line. Offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'.

Speed Humps Installation Notes
1. Speed humps shall be installed only when authorized by LADOT. Installations shall conform to the latest revision of LADOT Specification No. 51-008-003.
2. All asphalt concrete pavement shall conform to the most recent edition of the Standard Specification for Public Works Construction Section 302-5.
3. Speed humps shall not be placed over maintenance covers, watergates, junction chambers, etc.
4. Edge of speed humps should be 5 ft. or more from edge of driveway or catch basin.
5. Spacing between humps may vary. Exact locations and type of speed humps and sign locations shall be determined by LADOT.
6. Asphalt joins shall be accomplished by feather-edging.
7. The height of the speed hump shall not be less than 2 5/8 inch, and shall not exceed a tolerance of +1/4 inch.

Type I Speed Hump Marking (Chevron I)
Typical dimensions: 8' marking width, offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'. Chevron stripe dimensions 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1'. Hump spans driving lane W each side of the centerline, with a 12" taper at each gutter edge. Hump extent across the lane 12' with 4.5' from the flow line shown. Edge of gutter and flow line as labeled. See Page 1 for Section A-A.

Section B-B
Type I Speed Hump, 2 5/8" high by 12' long. 6' typical profile from 0 at the start to the 2.62" (2 5/8") crest, with heights at 6" typical stations of 0.42", 0.80", 1.15", 1.46", 1.73", 1.97", 2.17", 2.34", 2.46", 2.55", 2.61" and 2.62".

Type II Speed Hump Marking (Chevron II)
Typical dimensions as for Type I. Offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'. Hump spans driving lane W each side of the centerline, with a 12" taper at each gutter edge. Chevron dimension 5' as shown. See Page 1 for Section A-A.

Section C-C
Type II Speed Hump, 2 5/8" high by 22' long.

title: Raised Crosswalks
summary: Standard details for raised crosswalks with bicycle ramps across a bike lane, including approach and departure ramps, Chevron III and Chevron IV markings, and the sign assemblies for advance warning. The flat top is at least 10 ft wide and should match the connecting sidewalk or path. Ramps are at least 6 ft long with a 12.5% maximum slope. Sheet 3 shows a raised side street crosswalk at a standard curb ramp with optional green bicycle crossing.

sheets.notes:
Plan and section dimensions: 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1'. 6' min approach ramp. 10' min crosswalk (see Note 1). 6' min departure ramp. 4.5' flat top. 12.5% max. slope.
Raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III) on travel lane. Bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV) centered in lane. Bicycle ramp centered in lane. Bike lane and sidewalk shown. Culvert markings as needed. 3 flexible delineators on lane line spaced 20' on center. 8" minimum white edgeline. 20' typ.

Raised crosswalk marking and signs
Chevron III marking, typ., see standard detail. Advanced warning pavement marking, see standard detail S-509.0, see Note 2. Crosswalk sign assembly and advance sign assembly, see Note 2. Advanced sign posting locations C**. Curb ramp and humps shown.

Raised crosswalk sign assemblies
Crosswalk assembly: W11-2 or W11-15 with W16-7P and W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK). Advance assembly: W13-1 advisory speed, W16-9P (AHEAD), W17-1bP.

Advisory speed plaques
W13-1 (15 MPH), W13-1 (20 MPH), W13-1 (25 MPH), W13-1 (30 MPH). Use as appropriate for the raised crosswalk design speed.

Notes
1. The width of the top of raised crosswalks should match the width of the connecting sidewalk, shared use path, or desired crosswalk, but not less than 10' in width.
2. The placement of advanced warning signs and markings shall follow the guidance for advanced sign posting (C**) shown on S-481.0.
3. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 600 for raised crossing details.

Raised side street crosswalk
Shows a depressed corner and standard curb ramp, a 10' raised crosswalk marked by Chevron III (see Sheet 1), and a 10' bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV, see Sheet 1). 24" white crosswalk lines and 12" white crosswalk lines as labeled. Bicycle yield line and limit line (if needed). Bicycle crossing marking with optional solid green colored pavement.

title: Lane Reduction
summary: Typical signs and pavement markings for a lane reduction (lane drop), based on MUTCD Section 3B.09 and Figure 3B-12(CA). It shows the permanent lane drop and two peak-period cases, a peak-period lane that becomes an all-day parking lane and a full-time lane that becomes a peak-period lane. Table 1 gives the advance placement distance d and taper rate by posted speed, using posted speed plus 5 mph, for example 450 ft and 15:1 for a 25 mph road. W9-1 and W4-2 signs are used, with a plate when the lane is peak-period only.

sheets.notes:
Typical Signs and Lane Reduction Markings - Reference MUTCD Section 3B.09 and Figure 3B-12(CA)
W9-1 placed at distance d upstream, W4-2 at d/4 from the start of the taper. Distances d/2 between arrows. 8" white line along the taper. 12" W diagonals. Taper, see Table 1. Parking lane or narrowed roadway at the end of the taper.

Peak period lane to all day parking lane
With a 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see Note 1) on W9-1 and W4-2. Tow Away No Stopping (peak hours only) before the taper, all day parking permitted beyond it. 8' parking lane (7' minimum). 8" white line and 12" W diagonals, taper see Table 1. Lane line and curb line as shown.

Full time lane to peak period lane
With an EXCEPT 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see Note 2) on W9-1 and W4-2. Tow Away No Stopping Any Time before the taper, Tow Away No Stopping (peak hours only) beyond it. Lane line and curb line as shown.

Table 1
Posted speed limit (mph) / posted speed limit plus 5 mph / d distance (feet) / d/4 (feet) / taper rate (minimum)
25 / 30 / 450 / 113 / 15:1
30 / 35 / 550 / 138 / 20.5:1
35 / 40 / 650 / 163 / 26.7:1
40 / 45 / 750 / 188 / 45:1
45 / 50 / 850 / 213 / 50:1
50 / 55 / 950 / 238 / 55:1
55 / 60 / 1100 / 275 / 60:1
"d" = Advance placement distance per MUTCD, Section 2C.05, Condition A. Taper rates and "d" distances shown are based on posted speed plus 5 mph. Where the 85% speed (critical speed) on the approach is determined to be equal or less than the posted speed, the table numbers for the next lower speed increment may be used.

Signs: W4-2, W9-1.

Notes:
1. Where the lane dropped is a peak period lane, the W9-1 and W4-2 signs shall be modified by the addition of a black-on-yellow sign plate below to indicate the hours during which the curb lane is used by moving traffic.
2. Where the lane drop is installed in advance of a parking lane which is used as a thru lane for peak period traffic, the W9-1 and W4-2 signs shall be modified by the addition of a black-on-yellow sign plate below to indicate the excepted hours during which the lane is continuous.

title: Mast Arm Mounted Street Name Signs
summary: Layout, size and material requirements for street name signs mounted on signal mast arms, including freeway ramp signs. Street name signs are 18 in high for one line and 30 in high for two lines, with white legend on blue background. Freeway ramp signs are 72 in by 24 in with white legend on green. Sheet 2 shows the sign bracket, banding and aluminum channel framing details.

sheets.notes:
A. Street Name Signs
One-line sign 18" high, two-line sign 30" high, with 12" from each end to the mounting brackets and length as required (see Note 4). Examples: "Jefferson Bl"; "Mulholland Dr" with left arrow and "Valley Circle Bl" with right arrow.
Notes
1. Legend size: 8" upper case, 6" lower case, Series "E" letters. 11-1/4" x 12-3/4" one-line arrow.
2. Color: white legend, blue background.
3. Reflectivity: high intensity letters on Super Engineer Grade background or reverse screening on high intensity sheeting.
4. Where the length of the sign blade would exceed 96" (generally 16 letters and spaces) the street name titles, "St", "Ave", "Bl", "Pl", "Dr", "Rd", etc. may be deleted.

B. Freeway Ramp Signs
Sign 72" wide by 24" high with 12" from each end to the mounting brackets. Example: left arrow, Interstate 405 shield, "North".
Notes
1. Legend size: 8" and 6" Series D capital letters. 11-1/4" x 12-3/4" one-line arrow. 18" high US, California or Interstate shield, as appropriate with proportional numbers.
2. Color: white legend, Warboys green (L.A. No. 1) background. Black on white US shield, white on green California shield, white on blue and red Interstate shield.
3. Reflectivity: high intensity letters on Super Engineer Grade or reverse screening on high intensity sheeting.

Typical placement (example: Jefferson Bl, on-ramp)
Mast arm sign bracket. Signfix medium section secured to back of sign with pop rivets at 6" spacing. Fiber lock nut. Banding. Side view shows the front of the sign, sign material .080" aluminum.

Notes:
1. For installation details see Std. Plan S-457.0.
2. For Signfix aluminum channel framing system details see Standard Plan S-476.0.

title: Exclusive Bus Lane Pavement Markings
summary: Typical BUS ONLY pavement markings for exclusive bus lanes, shown at an intersection with markings placed on the approaches and at bus turn lanes. Typical spacings are 18 ft for a turn arrow and 16 ft and 8 ft for the legend words. Markings are installed at the start of bus turn lanes, at the start and end of each block with a bus only curb lane, and mid-block where the block exceeds 700 ft. Concurrent-flow lanes are delineated by 8 in solid white lines.

sheets.notes:
Typical spacings (shown on each approach): 18', 16', 8', 8' and 16', 8' between the turn arrow, the ONLY legend and the BUS legend. 8" lines with reference to Note 5.

Notes
1. These pavement markings are supplementary to signing which regulates use of the exclusive bus lanes.
2. Install the "BUS ONLY" pavement markings at the beginning of bus turn lanes and at the beginning and ending of each block where there is a bus only curb lane.
3. Bus only turn lanes shall be supplemented with turn pavement arrows.
4. Contra-flow bus only lanes shall be supplemented with straight ahead direction pavement arrows.
5. Concurrent-flow bus only lanes shall be delineated by 8" solid white lines. For a part-time bus lane installation, which is used as a mixed flow lane during non-restricted hours, a 4" solid white line shall be used.
6. Bus only left turn pocket lanes shall have a closed entrance delineated by the extension of the 8" white barrier line.
7. Mid-block pavement markings for bus only curb lanes shall be installed where the block length exceeds 700 feet.
8. The "BUS ONLY" pavement markings shall conform to the 8' high Caltrans standard.
9. All markings shall be Alkyd-Based thermoplastic.

title: Crosswalk Alignment
summary: Guidance for aligning marked crosswalks relative to curb ramps at intersection corners. Case 1 covers bi-directional ramps and Case 2 covers uni-directional ramps, using offset dimensions A, B and C. Generally A and B are at least 2 ft and C is at most 7 ft, with C preferably 4 ft. A 15 ft crosswalk width is standard and 20 ft is used in high pedestrian areas.

sheets.notes:
Case 1: Bi-directional ramps
Curb, dimensions A, B and C shown.

Case 2: Uni-directional ramps
Curb, dimension C shown.

Notes
1. Crosswalk installations with an access ramp intended to serve Case 1 situations generally should be aligned so that A>2', B>2' and C<7'. However, if there is an all-day parking lane, a parallel approach right-turn lane or if the curb lane width for parallel through traffic is >14', the related A or B distance may be >0.
2. Countless combinations of existing intersectional angles, curb radii and ramp locations prevent selection of specific dimensions for A, B, and C in Case 1 situations. C should be set at a preferred 4' dimension wherever the criteria for A and B are met. However, at a right angle intersection with an existing ramp located at the M.C. and curb return radius of <17', C must be <4' in order for A and B to be the desired 2' minimum needed when through curb lanes are <14'. For a curb radius of 14', set C=3' so that A & B are equal to 2'. C dimensions for curb radii between 14' and 17' may be increased proportionately to 4'. For curb radii <13', set the C distance at the edge of gutter (generally 1' to 2') when curb lanes are <14'. With these smaller radii where curb lanes are >14', the A and B distances should be decreased to 0 to achieve a larger C dimension.
3. At intersections where street resurfacing, street widening, or channelization projects require reinstallation or modification of an existing crosswalk, all crosswalks at the intersection should be realigned to meet the criteria of Notes 1 and 2 above.
4. At curb returns without a ramp where a single ramp location would not meet the criteria of Note 1 above, unidirection ramps should be proposed, as shown in Case 2.
5. For Case 2 situations, C<2'.
6. A crosswalk width of 15' is standard. Use 20' in high pedestrian areas, or on the receptive leg of dual left turns.

title: Advance Turn Lanes
summary: Marking and signing for advance (added) turn lanes and trap lanes, where a through lane ends as a mandatory turn lane. Trap lanes are delineated by elephant tracks, starting about two blocks ahead of the turn but not less than 500 ft and not more than 1,300 ft. They are supplemented with W4-7 and W7-3A(CA) signs. Right-turn trap lanes end with a curved barrier line at least 100 ft long, and left-turn trap lanes need overhead signing.

sheets.notes:
Signs: W4-7, W7-3A(CA), and a RIGHT LANE MUST TURN RIGHT sign, see Note 3.

Notes:
1. The second (downstream) pavement marking is not mandatory if advance turn lane is 100' long or less. At locations where a right turn is prohibited at an intermediate intersection during limited hours, the pavement arrow at that intersection should be deleted.
2. Continuous through lanes that terminate as mandatory turn lanes and that are not otherwise regulated by the Vehicle Code, (commonly known as "Trap Lanes") shall be delineated by Elephant Tracks. The length of Elephant Tracking should be two blocks in advance of the mandatory turn, but not less than 500 feet and not more than 1,300 feet. This striping shall be supplemented with W4-7 and W7-3A(CA) signing. The W4-7 sign should be placed near the start of the Elephant Tracks.
3. Added turn lanes (i.e. having no continuity upstream) traversing through all intervening intersections shall be delineated by Elephant Tracking (lane drop markings) and pavement arrows as shown.
4. Trap Lanes should be considered where it is not feasible to drop a lane with the standard signing and pavement markings. They should terminate at arterial streets or freeway ramps.
5. Trapped lanes for left turns should have overhead signing.
6. Trapped lanes for right turns shall be terminated by a curved barrier line and separated from the adjacent through lane by a longitudinal line. Barrier lines for right-turn lanes should be 100' minimum.
7. Placement of arrows should also conform with Standard Plan S-456.0.

title: Location of Limit Lines and Crosswalks
summary: Cases showing where to place limit lines (stop bars) and crosswalks at intersections, with R1-1 stop signs, R9-3 and R13A(CA) signs, driveways and keep clear areas. Case 1 covers corners with and without access ramps, with the stop line a 5 ft minimum from the crossing. Case 2 shows a 35 ft minimum setback and alternates with an island or a large vehicle set back based on a turning template. The notes referenced by the cases are not on the sheets in this set, so only the visible dimensions and signs are recorded here.

sheets.notes:
Case 1 (with and without access ramps)
Property line, R1-1 stop signs at corners, see Note 2. Limit line 5' min.

Case 2
35' min. from the crosswalk to the limit line for the turning movement. See Note 3.

Case 2 Alternate, with island
35' min. Island as shown. See Note 3.

Case 2 Alternate, large vehicle set back
Base on turning template. WAIT HERE legend. See Note 3.

Case 9 and Case 10
KEEP CLEAR legend. R1-1, R10-6, R13A(CA), R9-3S, see Notes 11 and 12. 20' min. Dimension <20' as shown.

Case 11 and Case 12
R1-1 and R6-1 signs.

Case 13 and Case 14
See Notes 13, 14 and 15. 5' dimensions. 12" yellow line. W12-1. 5' min. WAIT HERE legend. Driveway.

Case 15
WAIT HERE legend. 5' from driveway. 2' white or yellow line. See Note 15.

title: Channelized Right Turns
summary: Five cases of channelized right turn control. Stop sign (Case 1) is used where the curb return radius is under 20 ft, pedestrian traffic is high, or visibility is restricted. Yield (Cases 2 and 3), merge (Case 4) and added lane (Case 5) operation depend on the radius and the available acceleration and merging distance. Tables 1 to 3 give S1, D1 and D2 for the merge case, and the added lane case needs an all-day receiving lane of 1/2 mile or more.

sheets.notes:
Case 1: Stop sign control (R1-1)
Note: Use stop sign operation where the curb return radius is less than 20 feet (10 miles per hour design speed), pedestrian traffic across the channelized right turn is high, cross-traffic visibility is restricted, or where the use of a yield sign has been shown to be inadequate.

Case 2: Yield sign control (R1-2)
Note: Use yield sign operation where the curb return radius is 20 feet (10 miles per hour design speed) or greater and pedestrian traffic across the channelized right turn is low.

Case 3: Yield sign control (see Note 1)
Detail A: 12 in. and 24 in. markings as shown.
Notes
1. Use yield sign operation where the available distance "x" for acceleration and merging is less than "D", as determined by the tables in Case 4.
2. Installation of the yield limit line is optional.
3. An optional added location for a crosswalk is where the yield sign is shown near the end of the island. If added, stop sign control should be considered. If yield sign control is retained then the crosswalk should have ladder markings as shown on sheet 1.

Case 4: Merge operation
D = Minimum distance necessary for accelerating and merging.
D1 = Minimum distance necessary for accelerating from point x at the initial speed, S1, to point y at the speed limit, S2. See Tables 1 and 2. Consideration should be given to using a design speed greater than the speed limit where higher speeds are known to occur.
D2 = Minimum distance necessary for merging maneuver at speed S2. See Table 3.
Notes
1) Use merge operation where the available distance for acceleration and merging equals or exceeds "D".
2) The length of lane line within D is discretionary.
3) Where it is desired to provide traffic signal control for pedestrians to cross the channelized right turn, the following shall apply:
a. Omit the W11-2 sign; and
b. Omit ladder markings in crosswalk.
c. Provide pedestrian heads across the channelized right turn; and
d. Control the channelized right turn with three-arrow signal heads; and
e. Omit reference to Table 1; and
f. Measure D1 from diagonal crosswalk; and
g. S1 = 0 at crosswalk.
4) Install a second W4-1 sign on the right side if the median mounted W4-1 sign is not visible to merging traffic.
Signs: W4-1, W11-2 (fluorescent yellow-green), W16-7P. 50' min. shown on plan.

Case 5: Added lane operation
Notes
1) Use added lane operation where the receiving lane is available all day and equals or exceeds 1/2 mile in length.
2) Where it is desired to provide traffic signal control for pedestrians to cross the channelized right turn, the following shall apply:
a. Omit the W11-2 sign; and
b. Omit ladder markings in crosswalk.
c. Provide pedestrian heads across the channelized right turn; and
d. Control the channelized right turn with three-arrow signal heads.
3) Install a second W4-3 sign on the right side if the median mounted W4-3 sign is not visible to merging traffic.
All day lane 1/2 mile minimum. Signs: W4-3, W11-2 (fluorescent yellow-green), W16-7P. 2' white or yellow line, 5' C-C.

title: Channelized Right Turns with Raised Crosswalks
summary: Details for a raised crosswalk across a channelized right turn, with and without a bike lane. Drivers yield at a YIELD HERE TO line ahead of the crosswalk, with R1-5L/R1-5R signs and RAISED CROSSWALK AHEAD assemblies. The raised crosswalk marking is Chevron III from S-483.1. Approach and departure ramps are at least 6 ft long, or 9 ft where WB-50 trucks or buses are expected, and the crossing is at least 20 ft from the through lane. Green colored pavement is recommended for the bike crossing.

sheets.notes:
Pedestrian island, channelized right turn, raised crosswalk
Raised crosswalk, see S-483.1. Raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III), see S-483.1. Raised crosswalk ahead assembly with W17-1bP. R1-1, see S-494.0. Marked pedestrian crosswalk, typ., see detail S-481.1. 12" stop line, yield line, white edge line. R1-5L and R1-5R with W17-1bP (YIELD HERE TO crosswalk). W11-2. 10' min. approach ramp and departure ramp, see Note 4. 20' min. 2' white or yellow line, 5' C-C.

Raised crosswalk ahead assembly detail: RAISED CROSSWALK AHEAD with W17-1bP.

Pedestrian island, channelized right turn, raised crosswalk with bike lane
Raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III), see S-483.1. Grass buffer, sidewalk and bike lane. 20' min. 2' white or yellow line, 5' C-C. 2' green colored bicycle crossing, 5' C-C beside the pedestrian crossing. Raised crosswalk ahead assembly. R1-5R MOD with W17-1bP and R1-5L MOD with W17-1bP (YIELD HERE TO). Marked bike lane with bike symbol, see Notes. Marked pedestrian crosswalk, typ., see S-481.1. R1-1. Bike lane symbol, typ. White edge lines, typ. Green colored surface recommended, see Note 2. 12" stop line. Approach ramp and departure ramp, see Note 4. 10' min.

Notes:
1. Bike lane symbols are recommended to clarify the intended operation of the bike lane space.
2. Optional use of green colored pavement to enhance visibility and conspicuity of bicycle lane. Green colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of the bicycle lane or for only a portion (or portions) of the bicycle lane. All green colored pavement should comply with FHWA Interim Approval for Optional Use of Green Colored Pavement for Bike Lanes (IA-14) and approved by LADOT.
3. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 100 and Detail 600 for pedestrian/bicyclist island and raised crosswalk details.
4. Approach and departure ramps should be a minimum of 6' in length. Where WB-50's or buses are expected the ramp length should be 9' minimum.
